tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf

# gh-1012: Flaky: scheduled_indicator_test scheduled-follow-up timing flake under runner load — quarantined, fix + re-enable

## Description

## Evidence
- fa CI run on branch `ai/gh-957`, job **PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard 0/3)** at 14:18Z fails on **"a scheduled follow-up shows on top of the working row, persists while idle, and clears when it fires"** in `test/integration/scheduled_indicator_test.dart`.
- Unrelated to the PR under test (#959 drops CRAP excludes) — the failure is a timing flake: the scheduled-indicator/schedule waits (`waitForText` 30s/45s windows) do not land in time under validation runner variance.
- Failure class: TimeoutException on the indicator/fire waits; the test is inherently timing-sensitive (20s-out reminder, settle, fire, clear) and reddens the pty-integration leg.

## Quarantine
- Scope: single test case quarantined via the repo's `skip:` convention (same as gh-982 / gh-1007); the rest of the file still runs.

## Required to close
1. Diagnose and harden the schedule/indicator timing under runner load (deterministic clock or longer/poller waits).
2. Remove the skip and verify the test is stable across repeated CI validation runs.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes …

`UnifiedModelPickerPage` (applies on the ACTIVE provider, key resolved
  via the registry). The `ProvidersSection` rows carry the SAME brand mark
  the add-provider picker shows — `providerMarkKey` (preset) /
  `providerMarkKeyForBaseUrl` (custom provider, URL-matched: codemie
  marker, openrouter.ai, ollama.com, generativelanguage…, else `custom`) in
  `provider_marks.dart` — and never a current-provider check; every row
  trails a chevron into the editor. The provider editor
  (`ProviderEditorPage`) owns
  name/URL/key; the model id is a button-style row (icon + current model +
  chevron, mirroring the `TaskModelsSection` rows) opening
  `MediaSlotModelPage` with `slot: null` DIRECTLY (no provider-picker step)
  for a transient provider entry built from the CURRENT form values — the
  edited provider keeps its id so the stored key resolves, and a freshly
  typed (unsaved) key rides the page's `apiKeyOverride` (preset mode falls
  back to the stored preset key). The editor's `modelsFetcher` is a test
  seam threaded through `ProvidersSection`/`AddProviderPresetPickerPage`/
  `pushProviderEditor`. The media slots AND the agent-role rows
  (`TaskModelsSection`: Quick model / Subagents model) share the ONE
  two-step flow — `MediaSlotProviderPickerPage` → `MediaSlotModelPage`
  with `slot: null` for roles (no voice field, no capability chips,
  dial-aware provider kind) — so provider→model picking can never drift
  between settings surfaces. The endpoint fetch
  goes through the core `fetchModelsForEndpoint` dispatch (DIAL deployments
  / CodeMie marker / OpenAI `/models`); the legacy two-step
  `DefaultModelProviderPickerPage`/`DefaultModelPickerPage` and the
  text-field `TaskRoleConfigPage` are gone.
  The chat leaf widgets live there too (`lib/src/chat/`): the Markdown
  style/sandbox image resolver (`markdown_style.dart`), the inline
  audio/video players (`media_player.dart`), the approval/ask/
  secret-request sheets, the
  transcript message tile (`chat_message_tile.dart`), the composer
  (`chat_composer.dart` — file/gallery/camera picking through the
  `FaChatHost.uploadPicker`/`galleryPicker`/`cameraPicker` hooks, voice
  input through `FaChatHost.voiceInput`; desktop keys: Shift+Enter inserts
  a newline (a Focus ancestor swallows the key before the text-input plugin
  turns it into `send`), Cmd/Ctrl+V is smart paste — a clipboard image
  (via the `FaChatHost.clipboardImageReader` hook) or long/multi-line text
  is staged as an `uploads/` attachment chip, short single-line text pastes
  inline), and the single-service chat
  screen (`fa_chat_screen.dart` — `FaChatScreen(service:, features:,
  title:, settingsBuilder:, fileBrowserBuilder:, composerBuilder:)`),
  plus the upload helpers
  (`upload_utils.dart`), the media tool-name constants
  (`media_tool_names.dart`), and the brand glyphs
  (`fa_glyphs.dart` — `FaAttachGlyph`, the SVG attach icon used by the
  composer, `FaModelGlyph`, the AI-chip icon leading the provider editor's
  model row, and `FaAiAvatar`, the `>_` squircle used as the assistant
  avatar in `chat_message_tile.dart`) —
  localized via `FaChatStrings` (en/ru defaults, `FaChatStringsScope`
  override), analytics via the `FaChatHost.track` hook, backend surface is
  the `FaChatService` interface (which `AgentService` implements;
  `ApprovalModeSelector` needs only the
  `FaApprovalModeController` slice).
  The trajectory ledger UI lives in `lib/src/trajectory/` (issue #25
  redesign): `TrajectoryController` (view-state owner — debounced
  snapshot updates, turn/assistant folds, the four timeline projections
  with selection, record selection, throttled search),
  `TrajectoryScreen` (the full-screen trajectory page: wide canvases
  `>= kWideLayoutBreakpoint` push it as a master-detail route from the
  chat app bar; narrow canvases swap it in as the chat screen's body via
  the Chat | Trajectory segmented switcher — controller state lives at
  screen level so the swap never loses scroll, selection, or filters),
  `TrajectoryHeader` (title + session stamp, stat pills, the search
  field with match position and prev/next navigation, the ledger filter
  chips, and the export overflow menu that copies the session as
  JSON/Markdown to the clipboard), `TrajectoryBody` (header above the
  ledger; wide splits ledger ~55% / details ~45% into
  `TrajectoryDetailsPane`, narrow keeps the tap-for-details sheet),
  `TrajectoryView` (control strip + Gantt timeline strip + ledger of
  two-line expandable selectable rows with per-row copy and injectable
  table/timeline builder seams), the details surface (`showTrajectoryDetails`
  sheet narrow / persistent pane wide: tab set per record kind with
  empty tabs hidden, a Request tab for outbound model payloads, per-tab
  copy, highlighted Raw view; session-scoped last-tab restore,
  `resetTrajectoryTabHistory()` test seam), and `FaTrajectoryPanel`
  for hosts that feed their own stream via `TrajectoryServiceFeed`
  (broadcast snapshot stream that replays `latest` to new listeners).
  `TrajectoryTimeline` draws the Gantt: time ruler + lane labels, three
  fixed lanes (0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools), a
  live pulse on the in-progress span, and the whole strip hidden when
  the session is untimed.
  Strings: `TrajectoryStrings` en/ru + `TrajectoryStringsScope`. Golden
  baselines: `test/trajectory/golden/` (regenerate with
  `flutter test test/trajectory/golden/ --update-goldens`, verify without
  the flag) — `golden_test_setup.dart` loads the real `Inter` and
  `JetBrainsMono` families from `test/assets/fonts/` (test-only copies
  of flutter_app's bundled TTFs; the package itself ships no font
  assets) plus the bundled MaterialIcons font, so goldens render real
  glyphs; review every changed PNG after regenerating.
  Package strings live in `FaUiStrings`
  (en/ru defaults resolved from the locale, host-overridable via
  `FaUiStringsScope`) — never the app's gen-l10n. App-level concerns are
  injected: the active connection is the `FaChatConnection` interface,
  on-device engine routes are `FaOnDeviceRoute` builders, the apply
  callback carries `FaChatModelConfig`, and named-key resolution goes
  through the `FaUiHost.keyResolver` hook. `flutter_app` consumes it via
  path dep + thin `export` shims at the old paths; the app's
  `lib/ui/screens/providers_section.dart` additionally keeps a
  `DefaultChatModelSection` ADAPTER (old constructor) wiring `AgentService`,
  `LastConnectionStore`, and the on-device engines into the package flow.
- `flutter_app/` — Flutter chat example. Layout: `lib/main.dart`

  shim re-exporting the fa_ui theme; `markdown_style.dart`, `screens/`,

  `lib/services/` (agent service, stores, upload, secrets, project mount,

Now I have a full understanding of the mechanics. Timing analysis of the test:

1. `t=0`: spawn. Boot (JIT `dart bin/fah.dart`) — under load can take 15-40s.
2. Test sends text immediately (buffered by PTY).
3. Turn 1 round 1 → mock schedule call → tool executes → record created (dueMs = now+20s) → `[sched] in 20s: check the build` + `_pushScheduledStatus` → indicator `⏰ 1 scheduled · next in 20s`.
4. Turn 1 round 2 → "turn-complete".
5. Test: waits `⏰ 1 scheduled` (30s from t≈0) — must cover BOOT + round 1. **← flake point 1: unbounded boot inside a 30s window.**
6. Waits `turn-complete` (30s).
7. settle 600ms → **assert indicator still on screen** — must happen before the record fires AND the indicator clears. **← flake point 2: if boot+turn > ~20s, the record fires mid-wait; delivery happens mid-run via the steering poll → record removed → indicator cleared → assert FAILS.** Also the `[sched] fired:` line arrives before the test even starts waiting for it (fine), and the wake turn... actually when busy, mail delivery doesn't start a wake; it lands via the steering drain mid-run or turn-end. The record is consumed at drain time.

Hmm wait — actually there's an even nastier variant of flake point 2: if the record is consumed mid-run by the steering poll, the mail text `[scheduled] check the build` enters the CURRENT run as steering. The wake is not a separate turn. Whatever — indicator clears.

8. Waits `[sched] fired:` (45s from t≈7+). Fire at dueMs = schedTime+20s. **← flake point 3: if the record already fired during step 6/7 (boot > 20s), `[sched] fired:` is already in the raw buffer — fine, contains-match. Actually this makes the fired-wait ROBUST (raw history). But then...**
9. `expect(mock.bodies.any(contains('[scheduled]')))` — the mail must reach the MODEL. If the record fired mid-run (while busy), the steering drain delivered it as steering in the CURRENT turn — the request body WOULD contain it. If it fired while idle, the wake turn carries it. Either way OK.
10. Poll for indicator clear (30s) — screen-based.

So the dominant flake: **boot time is unbounded and sits inside the 30s `⏰ 1 scheduled` window AND competes with the fixed 20s fire delay.** Under a loaded validation runner, boot+round1 > 30s → TimeoutException on the indicator wait (exactly the ticket's evidence), and boot+turn > 20s → the persist-while-idle assertion sees a cleared indicator.

The fix, following the ticket's "deterministic clock or longer/poller waits":

1. **Wait for boot FIRST** (`waitForBoot()` — 90s default), then send the prompt. This takes the boot out of the indicator window entirely. After boot, schedule→indicator is ~1-2s (local mock).

2. **Make the fire-vs-idle race deterministic**: increase the reminder delay from 20s to something with a much larger margin, e.g. 90s? That makes the test take 90s+. Hmm. Alternatively keep 20s — after boot, the whole turn-1 sequence is fast (mock is local, responds in ms), so schedule→settle-assert is ~2-4s, leaving 16s+ of margin. But under runner load, even post-boot turns can stall (TUI frames, event loop contention with the test's own polling every 50ms... that's light).

Actually — hmm, let me think about what "deterministic" could mean here. Could we avoid the wall-clock 20s entirely? The delay comes from the mock's scripted tool arguments. The CLI schedules per that. We could shorten the delay to e.g. 12s and assert persist-while-idle earlier... no, shrinking delays makes it worse.

Better: **derive the persist assertion from the indicator itself** — the ETA row shows `· next in 20s`; when the countdown expires it shows `· due now`. Not needed.

The cleanest robust approach:
- Boot first (removes unbounded boot from all windows).
- Keep 20s delay (bounded fire: schedule+20s; the fire wait window of 45s from ~schedule+3s is 28s+ generous; and the raw-history contains-match means even a missed-on-screen fire is caught).
- Extend the indicator wait window a bit (30s → 60s) as extra safety for post-boot stalls under load (costs nothing in the happy path — poll returns as soon as the text appears).
- Extend the fire wait 45s → 90s? Also free in the happy path. The @Timeout is 5 minutes; total worst case: boot 90 + indicator 60 + fire 90 + clear 30 + margins ≈ under 5m. Happy path: boot ~5-15s + 2s + 20s + ~2s ≈ 30-40s.

Race: fire can clear the indicator between the settle and the expect — only if the fire lands in that ~600ms window, i.e. schedule+20s ≈ settle time. After boot-first, that has ~16s margin — fine. But we can make it robust anyway: before asserting persistence, assert the indicator shows `next in` (i.e. the record is still pending with ETA) — hmm, the ETA renders whole minutes? No — `formatDelay` renders `20s` for sub-minute. So the row reads `⏰ 1 scheduled · next in 20s`, later `· next in 1s`?? Let me check formatDelay: seconds granularity → `next in 15s`, etc. The minute-boundary tick repaints, but repaints don't matter for contains.

That assertion both proves persistence and proves it hasn't fired. But careful: at render time the ETA could be `· due now` if dueMs <= now. With a 20s delay and settle at +2-4s, `next in` holds.     # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need

    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate

    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes …

`UnifiedModelPickerPage` (applies on the ACTIVE provider, key resolved
  via the registry). The `ProvidersSection` rows carry the SAME brand mark
  the add-provider picker shows — `providerMarkKey` (preset) /
  `providerMarkKeyForBaseUrl` (custom provider, URL-matched: codemie
  marker, openrouter.ai, ollama.com, generativelanguage…, else `custom`) in
  `provider_marks.dart` — and never a current-provider check; every row
  trails a chevron into the editor. The provider editor
  (`ProviderEditorPage`) owns
  name/URL/key; the model id is a button-style row (icon + current model +
  chevron, mirroring the `TaskModelsSection` rows) opening
  `MediaSlotModelPage` with `slot: null` DIRECTLY (no provider-picker step)
  for a transient provider entry built from the CURRENT form values — the
  edited provider keeps its id so the stored key resolves, and a freshly
  typed (unsaved) key rides the page's `apiKeyOverride` (preset mode falls
  back to the stored preset key). The editor's `modelsFetcher` is a test
  seam threaded through `ProvidersSection`/`AddProviderPresetPickerPage`/
  `pushProviderEditor`. The media slots AND the agent-role rows
  (`TaskModelsSection`: Quick model / Subagents model) share the ONE
  two-step flow — `MediaSlotProviderPickerPage` → `MediaSlotModelPage`
  with `slot: null` for roles (no voice field, no capability chips,
  dial-aware provider kind) — so provider→model picking can never drift
  between settings surfaces. The endpoint fetch
  goes through the core `fetchModelsForEndpoint` dispatch (DIAL deployments
  / CodeMie marker / OpenAI `/models`); the legacy two-step
  `DefaultModelProviderPickerPage`/`DefaultModelPickerPage` and the
  text-field `TaskRoleConfigPage` are gone.
  The chat leaf widgets live there too (`lib/src/chat/`): the Markdown
  style/sandbox image resolver (`markdown_style.dart`), the inline
  audio/video players (`media_player.dart`), the approval/ask/
  secret-request sheets, the
  transcript message tile (`chat_message_tile.dart`), the composer
  (`chat_composer.dart` — file/gallery/camera picking through the
  `FaChatHost.uploadPicker`/`galleryPicker`/`cameraPicker` hooks, voice
  input through `FaChatHost.voiceInput`; desktop keys: Shift+Enter inserts
  a newline (a Focus ancestor swallows the key before the text-input plugin
  turns it into `send`), Cmd/Ctrl+V is smart paste — a clipboard image
  (via the `FaChatHost.clipboardImageReader` hook) or long/multi-line text
  is staged as an `uploads/` attachment chip, short single-line text pastes
  inline), and the single-service chat
  screen (`fa_chat_screen.dart` — `FaChatScreen(service:, features:,
  title:, settingsBuilder:, fileBrowserBuilder:, composerBuilder:)`),
  plus the upload helpers
  (`upload_utils.dart`), the media tool-name constants
  (`media_tool_names.dart`), and the brand glyphs
  (`fa_glyphs.dart` — `FaAttachGlyph`, the SVG attach icon used by the
  composer, `FaModelGlyph`, the AI-chip icon leading the provider editor's
  model row, and `FaAiAvatar`, the `>_` squircle used as the assistant
  avatar in `chat_message_tile.dart`) —
  localized via `FaChatStrings` (en/ru defaults, `FaChatStringsScope`
  override), analytics via the `FaChatHost.track` hook, backend surface is
  the `FaChatService` interface (which `AgentService` implements;
  `ApprovalModeSelector` needs only the
  `FaApprovalModeController` slice).
  The trajectory ledger UI lives in `lib/src/trajectory/` (issue #25
  redesign): `TrajectoryController` (view-state owner — debounced
  snapshot updates, turn/assistant folds, the four timeline projections
  with selection, record selection, throttled search),
  `TrajectoryScreen` (the full-screen trajectory page: wide canvases
  `>= kWideLayoutBreakpoint` push it as a master-detail route from the
  chat app bar; narrow canvases swap it in as the chat screen's body via
  the Chat | Trajectory segmented switcher — controller state lives at
  screen level so the swap never loses scroll, selection, or filters),
  `TrajectoryHeader` (title + session stamp, stat pills, the search
  field with match position and prev/next navigation, the ledger filter
  chips, and the export overflow menu that copies the session as
  JSON/Markdown to the clipboard), `TrajectoryBody` (header above the
  ledger; wide splits ledger ~55% / details ~45% into
  `TrajectoryDetailsPane`, narrow keeps the tap-for-details sheet),
  `TrajectoryView` (control strip + Gantt timeline strip + ledger of
  two-line expandable selectable rows with per-row copy and injectable
  table/timeline builder seams), the details surface (`showTrajectoryDetails`
  sheet narrow / persistent pane wide: tab set per record kind with
  empty tabs hidden, a Request tab for outbound model payloads, per-tab
  copy, highlighted Raw view; session-scoped last-tab restore,
  `resetTrajectoryTabHistory()` test seam), and `FaTrajectoryPanel`
  for hosts that feed their own stream via `TrajectoryServiceFeed`
  (broadcast snapshot stream that replays `latest` to new listeners).
  `TrajectoryTimeline` draws the Gantt: time ruler + lane labels, three
  fixed lanes (0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools), a
  live pulse on the in-progress span, and the whole strip hidden when
  the session is untimed.
  Strings: `TrajectoryStrings` en/ru + `TrajectoryStringsScope`. Golden
  baselines: `test/trajectory/golden/` (regenerate with
  `flutter test test/trajectory/golden/ --update-goldens`, verify without
  the flag) — `golden_test_setup.dart` loads the real `Inter` and
  `JetBrainsMono` families from `test/assets/fonts/` (test-only copies
  of flutter_app's bundled TTFs; the package itself ships no font
  assets) plus the bundled MaterialIcons font, so goldens render real
  glyphs; review every changed PNG after regenerating.
  Package strings live in `FaUiStrings`
  (en/ru defaults resolved from the locale, host-overridable via
  `FaUiStringsScope`) — never the app's gen-l10n. App-level concerns are
  injected: the active connection is the `FaChatConnection` interface,
  on-device engine routes are `FaOnDeviceRoute` builders, the apply
  callback carries `FaChatModelConfig`, and named-key resolution goes
  through the `FaUiHost.keyResolver` hook. `flutter_app` consumes it via
  path dep + thin `export` shims at the old paths; the app's
  `lib/ui/screens/providers_section.dart` additionally keeps a
  `DefaultChatModelSection` ADAPTER (old constructor) wiring `AgentService`,
  `LastConnectionStore`, and the on-device engines into the package flow.
- `flutter_app/` — Flutter chat example. Layout: `lib/main.dart`
  (entrypoint + BootstrapScreen: auto-connects the restored last connection
  when its key resolves, else SetupScreen), `lib/ui/` (`app_theme.dart` —
  shim re-exporting the fa_ui theme; `markdown_style.dart`, `screens/`,
  `widgets/`),
  `lib/services/` (agent service, stores, upload, secrets, project mount,
  vision, `theme_controller.dart` theme-mode persistence + `FahThemeScope`;
  `session_keys_store.dart`/`keychain_store.dart`/`provider_registry.dart`/
  `media_models_store.dart`/`vision_models.dart` are shim re-exports of the
  fa_ui stores), `lib/sandbox/` (env,
  shells, wasm, git, fs persistence), feature dirs
  `lib/apps|gemma|webllm|transformers_js|l10n/`. All lib-internal imports
  are absolute `package:fa/...` — no relative imports.
- `flutter_app/lib/ui/markdown_style.dart` (shim re-export of
  `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/chat/markdown_style.dart`) — beyond
  `fahMarkdownStyleSheet`: `SandboxImageResolver`/`fahSandboxImageBuilder`
  render markdown images with sandbox paths (`![alt](generated/x.png)`,
  leading `/` stripped) by loading bytes via `env.readBinaryFile` (memoized
  per surface, dim placeholder on failure, tap → `showFahImagePreview`
  fullscreen dialog); wired into the chat screen and the Fa chat overlay
  markdown. `generate_image` tool tiles also render the saved image inline
  (path parsed from the result text, which itself teaches the model the
  `![image](<path>)` convention).
- `flutter_app/lib/ui/widgets/media_player.dart` (shim re-export of
  `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/chat/media_player.dart`) — inline audio/video
  playback of sandb…

Potential flake sources:

**A. The settle-and-persist check race:** After `turn-complete` arrives, the test settles 300ms and expects the indicator. If the whole turn (schedule → turn-complete) took longer than 20s under load, the reminder may fire right at `settleMs` time, meaning delivery consumes the record and the indicator may clear BEFORE the persist assert — actually the clear happens when the wake turn drains. Hmm, but the delivery → indicator clear path: `onFired` fires `[sched] fired:` and pushes status; the record is removed on send. So the indicator could clear quickly. **B. The fire wait `waitForText('[sched] fired:', 45s)`:** `[sched] fired:` is a dim line written to the TUI... wait, `io.writeln` in TUI mode — what does it do? In TUI mode, `io.writeln` prints above the frame? The raw output should contain it. `waitForText` checks raw output OR screen. The test flow again:
1. `⏰ 1 scheduled` appears when the record is created (during the run).

Failure mode per ticket: "TimeoutException on the indicator/fire waits" — the `waitForText` for `⏰ 1 scheduled` or `[sched] fired:`.

Now — under runner load, where can 30s/45s not be enough?

**Boot time**: `dart bin/fah.dart` under JIT on a loaded runner can take a long time to boot. The test does NOT wait for boot before sending text. `harness.sendText('set a reminder')` right after spawn. The keystrokes are buffered by the PTY and processed once the TUI is up. Boot could take 15-30s under load (JIT compile of the whole CLI). Then the turn: POST 1 → schedule tool → POST 2 → turn-complete. That could push `⏰ 1 scheduled` wait near 30s+.

Actually wait — there's something even more subtle. The `schedule_message` mock schedules "20s". The fire happens 20s after the record was created. Now the `[sched] fired:` line — I need to check `ScheduledMessageQueue` for the fire path: does `[sched] fired:` print BEFORE the wake turn or after? Look at the sweep: it delivers the record (sends to mailbox), then `onFired` is invoked... Let me check scheduled_message_queue.dart.

Also — CRITICAL: the fire timer legs are capped at 60s (maxTimerLeg). 20s fits. The sweep interval — hosts sweep on inbox ticks (2s) plus a timer. OK.

Another candidate: **the wake turn hijacks the assertion text**. When the reminder fires, a wake turn runs and the mock returns `turn-complete` AGAIN. But `waitForText('turn-complete')` already matched earlier... fine.

Hmm wait, actually, let me re-read the mock: `bodies.length == 1` → schedule call chunks; else text chunks. Sequence of POSTs:
1. Turn 1, round 1 → schedule call.
2. Turn 1, round 2 (after tool result) → "turn-complete" (text).
3. Wake turn round 1 → "turn-complete" again.

The wake turn carries the `[scheduled]` mail as a user message; the mock ignores request content except count. `mock.bodies.any((b) => b.contains('[scheduled]'))` — check that the wake request includes the mail text. The delivery happens as a system notice / user message in the wake run. OK.

Now, the ** TimeoutException on the indicator wait**. Which indicator wait — the first `⏰ 1 scheduled` (30s) or `[sched] fired:` (45s)?

Scenario for the FIRST wait failing: under load, boot takes >30s? That seems plausible on a loaded validation runner — the memory note says "TUI slash-command dispatch under `dart test` can take >10s to reach persistence callbacks". Boot + turn could exceed 30s. But other PTY tests use 90s boot waits (`waitForBoot` default 90s). This test has NO boot wait — it fires text at a not-yet-booted TUI, relying on PTY buffering.

Hmm wait — but there's something else! Look carefully at the FIRST wait: `waitForText('⏰ 1 scheduled', 30s)`. The schedule happens when the tool executes, ~10-20s after submit. Fine.

Then `waitForText('turn-complete', 30s)`: the run settles. THEN `waitForOutput(settleMs: 300)` — waits for 600ms of silence. Then `expect(screenText, contains('⏰ 1 scheduled'))` — SCREEN check.

**Now the killer race**: the reminder fires 20s after creation. The turn can still be streaming when the reminder fires — if the run took >20s. Then during the settle+assert, the wake turn starts... The indicator stays until the record is consumed (on send). Actually when does the indicator CLEAR? `pendingSummary()` after the record file is removed on delivery. The sweep removes the record on send, then calls `onFired`. So the indicator clears almost immediately at fire time.

So if boot+turn1 takes >20s — which is EXACTLY what happens under runner load (that's the flake!) — then by the time the test reaches `expect(harness.screenText, contains('⏰ 1 scheduled'))`, the reminder has already fired and cleared → the persist assertion FAILS. But the ticket says the failure is TimeoutException... 

Hmm wait, actually re-read: if the reminder fires WHILE turn 1 is still streaming (before `turn-complete`), the wake can't start mid-run — the mail waits, and is delivered via the steering poll mid-run or at turn end. The `[sched] fired:` line prints at fire time regardless. And the record is consumed (removed) at delivery. Delivery mid-run: the steering drain consumes the record → indicator clears.

So under load with turn 1 > 20s:
- `turn-complete` wait: passes at, say, t=25s.
- settle 300ms.
- `expect(screenText contains('⏰ 1 scheduled'))`: indicator already cleared at t=20s → **FAIL here**. That's an expect failure, not TimeoutException.

OR the `waitForText('⏰ 1 scheduled', 30s)` itself: appears quickly when the tool runs (say t=12s). Fine.

OR: the indicator NEVER appears within 30s if boot+round1 > 30s.

Let me think about `[sched] fired:` failing (45s): fires at schedule+20s. If schedule at t=15s, fire at t=35s < 45s window (window starts after the settle, t≈26s → needs fire before t=71s). Fine unless the sweep is delayed.

Hmm OK. But the ticket says the failure was specifically on the test case with TimeoutException on indicator/fire waits. The evidence: "the scheduled-indicator/schedule waits (waitForText 30s/45s windows) do not land in time under validation runner variance."

So the fix should:
1. Make the reminder delay LONGER (or derive the fire timing robustly) so the "persists while idle" window is guaranteed.
2. Make the waits more robust: wait for boot first; use longer windows; poll the fire with the raw buffer (already); ensure the persist assert is race-free.
3. Possibly make the whole scenario deterministic by parsing the actual scheduled delay... The delay is fixed by the mock: 20s.

Better approach — make the test robust:
- Wait for boot (`waitForBoot`) before sending the prompt? The test sends text immediately; PTY buffers it. But to be safe under load, waiting for boot first removes the boot time from the 30s indicator window. Actually no — sending early is fine and faster; the waits are about the indicator appearing.

Real fix directions per the ticket: "deterministic clock or longer/poller waits".

Option A — deterministic: schedule with a delay that only starts counting when we're ready... can't; the mock controls delay. We control the mock! We can make the delay longer (e.g., 45s or 60s) so the fire is guaranteed to happen after the persist assert even under load. But then the fire wait needs a longer window (e.g., 120s), and the total test time grows. Currently the test takes ~25-30s (20s of which is the reminder wait). With a 45s delay it'd take ~50s. Acceptable for an integration test? The pty suite is nightly/validation-only. Hmm.

Option B — split the scenario: shorten the delay (e.g., 8s) and reorder assertions? No — persist-while-idle needs fire > idle-check.

Option C — drive the timing deterministically: the ETA row shows `· next in 20s`... not needed.

Option D — make the waits adaptive: instead of fixed 30s, wait for boot first (waitForBoot 90s), THEN send text, THEN wait for the indicator (30s from a booted state — round trip is fast since the mock is local). The boot is the long pole; everything after boot is fast (mock responds in ms; tool exec ms). With boot awaited first:
- indicator appears ~1-3s after send → 30s window is huge.
- turn-complete ~1-2s later.
- fire at +20s from schedule → `[sched] fired:` within 45s window easily.
- persist assert: fire is 20s away, settle+assert happen ~2s after schedule. Safe margin 18s.
- clear poll: 30s.

That converts the flake-prone "unbounded boot inside the indicator window" into a bounded fast path. The remaining load sensitivity: the 20s fire vs. the time between schedule and the persist assert — after boot, schedule→persist-assert is ~2-4s. Safe.

But wait — is `waitForBoot` usable here? It waits for `[Model]` in the banner + 400ms settle. Fine. But `sendText` before boot completes: in TUI mode keystrokes before the TUI is up... The PTY is in raw mode from the start; the CLI reads stdin once the TUI start…

Now I have a full understanding of the mechanics. Timing analysis of the test:

1. `t=0`: spawn. Boot (JIT `dart bin/fah.dart`) — under load can take 15-40s.

3. Turn 1 round 1 → mock schedule call → tool executes → record created (dueMs = now+20s) → `[sched] in 20s: check the build` + `_pushScheduledStatus` → indicator `⏰ 1 scheduled · next in 20s`.
4. Turn 1 round 2 → "turn-complete".
5. Test: waits `⏰ 1 scheduled` (30s from t≈0) — must cover BOOT + round 1. **← flake point 1: unbounded boot inside a 30s window.**
6. Waits `turn-complete` (30s).
7. settle 600ms → **assert indicator still on screen** — must happen before the record fires AND the indicator clears. **← flake point 2: if boot+turn > ~20s, the record fires mid-wait; delivery happens mid-run via the steering poll → record removed → indicator cleared → assert FAILS.** Also the `[sched] fired:` line arrives before the test even starts waiting for it (fine), and the wake turn... actually when busy, mail delivery doesn't start a wake; it lands via the steering drain mid-run or turn-end. The record is consumed at drain time.

8. Waits `[sched] fired:` (45s from t≈7+). Fire at dueMs = schedTime+20s. **← flake point 3: if the record already fired during step 6/7 (boot > 20s), `[sched] fired:` is already in the raw buffer — fine, contains-match. Actually this makes the fired-wait ROBUST (raw history). But then...**

  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the

  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf

{"path":"/tmp/gh1012_repeat.sh","content":"#!/usr/bin/env bash
# gh-1012 stability loop: run the re-enabled scheduled-indicator PTY test

set -u

runs=5
pass=0

  echo "=== run $i/$runs ==="

     -u FA_LOG_FILE -u FAH_PROVIDER -u FAH_MODEL -u FAH_SESSION_FILE \

    tail -40 /tmp/gh1012_run_$i.log
    exit 1
  fi
done
echo "stability: $pass/$runs passed"
"}

## Description

## Evidence
- fa CI run on branch `ai/gh-957`, job **PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard 0/3)** at 14:18Z fails on **"a scheduled follow-up shows on top of the working row, persists while idle, and clears when it fires"** in `test/integration/scheduled_indicator_test.dart`.

## Quarantine
- Scope: single test case quarantined via the repo's `skip:` convention (same as gh-982 / gh-1007); the rest of the file still runs.

## Required to close
1. Diagnose and harden the schedule/indicator timing under runner load (deterministic clock or longer/poller waits).
2. Remove the skip and verify the test is stable across repeated CI validation runs.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars

Now I have a full understanding of the mechanics. Timing analysis of the test:

1. `t=0`: spawn. Boot (JIT `dart bin/fah.dart`) — under load can take 15-40s.
2. Test sends text immediately (buffered by PTY).
3. Turn 1 round 1 → mock schedule call → tool executes → record created (dueMs = now+20s) → `[sched] in 20s: check the build` + `_pushScheduledStatus` → indicator `⏰ 1 scheduled · next in 20s`.
4. Turn 1 round 2 → "turn-complete".
5. Test: waits `⏰ 1 scheduled` (30s from t≈0) — must cover BOOT + round 1. **← flake point 1: unbounded boot inside a 30s window.**
6. Waits `turn-complete` (30s).
7. settle 600ms → **assert indicator still on screen** — must happen before the record fires AND the indicator clears. **← flake point 2: if boot+turn > ~20s, the record fires mid-wait; delivery happens mid-run via the steering poll → record removed → indicator cleared → assert FAILS.** Also the `[sched] fired:` line arrives before the test even starts waiting for it (fine), and the wake turn... actually when busy, mail delivery doesn't start a wake; it lands via the steering drain mid-run or turn-end. The record is consumed at drain time.

Hmm wait — actually there's an even nastier variant of flake point 2: if the record is consumed mid-run by the steering poll, the mail text `[scheduled] check the build` enters the CURRENT run as steering. The wake is not a separate turn. Whatever — indicator clears.

8. Waits `[sched] fired:` (45s from t≈7+). Fire at dueMs = schedTime+20s. **← flake point 3: if the record already fired during step 6/7 (boot > 20s), `[sched] fired:` is already in the raw buffer — fine, contains-match. Actually this makes the fired-wait ROBUST (raw history). But then...**
9. `expect(mock.bodies.any(contains('[scheduled]')))` — the mail must reach the MODEL. If the record fired mid-run (while busy), the steering drain delivered it as steering in the CURRENT turn — the request body WOULD contain it. If it fired while idle, the wake turn carries it. Either way OK.
10. Poll for indicator clear (30s) — screen-based.

So the dominant flake: **boot time is unbounded and sits inside the 30s `⏰ 1 scheduled` window AND competes with the fixed 20s fire delay.** Under a loaded validation runner, boot+round1 > 30s → TimeoutException on the indicator wait (exactly the ticket's evidence), and boot+turn > 20s → the persist-while-idle assertion sees a cleared indicator.

The fix, following the ticket's "deterministic clock or longer/poller waits":

1. **Wait for boot FIRST** (`waitForBoot()` — 90s default), then send the prompt. This takes the boot out of the indicator window entirely. After boot, schedule→indicator is ~1-2s (local mock).

2. **Make the fire-vs-idle race deterministic**: increase the reminder delay from 20s to something with a much larger margin, e.g. 90s? That makes the test take 90s+. Hmm. tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf

# gh-1012: Flaky: scheduled_indicator_test scheduled-follow-up timing flake under runner load — quarantined, fix + re-enable

## Description

## Evidence
- fa CI run on branch `ai/gh-957`, job **PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard 0/3)** at 14:18Z fails on **"a scheduled follow-up shows on top of the working row, persists while idle, and clears when it fires"** in `test/integration/scheduled_indicator_test.dart`.
- Unrelated to the PR under test (#959 drops CRAP excludes) — the failure is a timing flake: the scheduled-indicator/schedule waits (`waitForText` 30s/45s windows) do not land in time under validation runner variance.
- Failure class: TimeoutException on the indicator/fire waits; the test is inherently timing-sensitive (20s-out reminder, settle, fire, clear) and reddens the pty-integration leg.

## Quarantine
- Scope: single test case quarantined via the repo's `skip:` convention (same as gh-982 / gh-1007); the rest of the file still runs.

## Required to close
1. Diagnose and harden the schedule/indicator timing under runner load (deterministic clock or longer/poller waits).
2. Remove the skip and verify the test is stable across repeated CI validation runs.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes …
